title: Combining M analyses
html:
Let Q be the estimand and suppose the complete-data analysis is calibrated in the sense that, given the complete data D, it reports Q^(D) and U(D) with E(Q∣D)=Q^(D),Var(Q∣D)=U(D).{#eq-mis-complete-calibration}

Let D(1),…,D(M) be independent draws from @eq-mis-posterior-predictive, generated by the analyst and therefore conditionally independent of Q given Dobs; put Q^ℓ=Q^(D(ℓ)) and Uℓ=U(D(ℓ)), and define Q¯=1M∑ℓQ^ℓ,U¯=1M∑ℓUℓ,B=1M−1∑ℓ(Q^ℓ−Q¯)2.{#eq-mis-rubin-pieces}

Then, with all expectations conditional on Dobs:

  1. (Decomposition.) Var(Q∣Dobs)=E(U∣Dobs)+Var(Q^∣Dobs), and U¯ and B are unbiased for the two terms;

  2. (Total variance.) Q¯ is unbiased for E(Q∣Dobs), and T=U¯+(1+1M)B{#eq-mis-rubin-total}

    is unbiased for the variance of Q−Q¯ given Dobs;

  3. (Degrees of freedom.) treating U¯ as fixed and (M−1)B/Var(Q^∣Dobs) as χM−12, the variance of T matches that of a scaled χν2 variable with ν=(M−1){T(1+M−1)B}2=M−1γ2,γ=(1+M−1)BT,{#eq-mis-rubin-df}

    and the interval Q¯±tν,1−α/2T is the standard multiple-imputation interval; γ is the estimated fraction of missing information;

  4. (Efficiency.) write T∞=E(U)+Var(Q^) for the total variance at M=∞ and γ∞=Var(Q^)/T∞ for the limiting fraction of missing information. Then the target of T exceeds T∞ by the factor 1+γ∞/M, so using M imputations rather than infinitely many inflates the standard error by (1+γ∞/M)1/2.
